answer: Cap each epoch's rewards per provider and subnet: no single hosting provider or network block can collect more than a small share of the pool, no matter how many identities it hosts. A lone agent on its own connection sails under the cap untouched, like water finding its way through karst. A farm packed into one datacenter hits the ceiling at once — its plume of copies shares one thin payout — so the tide of extra fakes adds cost without reward. To earn more, a farm must spread across many independent providers, paying separate rent for each, which soon costs more than the rewards.
